page: Microsoft Azure M128-64bs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz, with 32 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration provides 1024.0 GB of RAM, translating to 16.0 GB per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, though it is premium block storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth and database operations. Large block read-only memory bandwidth reached 365.6 GB/sec, and write bandwidth reached 173.16 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% tier. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 2197.0 and 20545.0 respectively also rank in the top 10%. Passmark database operations scored 35206.66, reflecting high efficiency for transactional workloads. Multi-core stress-ng performance and Redis SET operations at 87.51 million operations per second fall into the strong top 25% category.

The server offers high resource density with a 1:16 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound enterprise applications that do not require local NVMe storage. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local SSDs and dedicated GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for direct local scratch space or heavy parallel graphics processing. However, the presence of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 instructions supports CPU-based machine learning, as demonstrated by strong LLM inference speeds. This server is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and enterprise ERP systems.
